questions.stem: The ABO blood group system was discovered by:

options.option_text: Charles Darwin during his evolution work
Karl Landsteiner around the year 1900
Louis Pasteur during his germ-theory work
Watson and Crick in 1953 with DNA work

questions.explanation: ABO blood group system — discovered by KARL LANDSTEINER in 1900 (Austria-USA). Nobel Prize 1930. Established that not all human blood is the same. Made transfusion safe. Discovered Rh factor in 1940 (with Wiener). Distractor 1 — Darwin's evolution. Distractor 3 — Pasteur's germ theory. Distractor 4 — DNA structure.

questions.stem: Among ABO blood groups, the UNIVERSAL DONOR (whose blood can be given to anyone in emergencies) is:

options.option_text: Group A positive blood type
Group O negative blood type
Group B positive blood type
Group AB positive blood type

questions.explanation: O NEGATIVE — universal donor. Lacks A and B antigens AND lacks Rh-D antigen → recipient's blood does NOT mount antibody attack. Used in emergency transfusion when blood type unknown. UNIVERSAL RECIPIENT — AB POSITIVE — has A, B antigens AND Rh-D, so it has no antibodies against any blood; can receive any blood type. Indian blood-type frequencies (approximate): O ~37%, B ~32%, A ~22%, AB ~9%; Rh+ ~95%, Rh− ~5%.

questions.stem: A person with blood group A has antigens of type A on RBCs and antibodies in plasma against:

options.option_text: Antigen A, against own type
Antigen B, against the other type
Both A and B antigens together
Neither A nor B antigens at all

questions.explanation: Blood group A — A antigen on RBCs; ANTI-B antibodies in plasma (would attack B-type RBCs). Group B — B antigen, ANTI-A antibodies. Group AB — both antigens, NEITHER antibody (universal recipient). Group O — NO antigens, BOTH anti-A AND anti-B antibodies (universal donor for ABO; cells lack A/B). Body doesn't make antibodies against its own antigens (self-tolerance) — Distractor 1 wrong. Distractor 3 wrong (would be O blood). Distractor 4 wrong (would be AB).

questions.stem: The Rh FACTOR was named after which animal in which it was first identified?

options.option_text: Rabbit, used in 1940 immunisation experiments
Rhesus macaque monkey, used by Landsteiner & Wiener
Roan horse, in 1930s veterinary research
Russian dog, in classical conditioning experiments

questions.explanation: Rh factor — named after RHESUS MACAQUE (Macaca mulatta) monkey. Landsteiner and Wiener (1937-40) used Rhesus macaque blood to immunise rabbits → produced antibodies that also reacted with ~85% of human RBCs (Rh-positive). Pivotal for understanding HEMOLYTIC DISEASE OF NEWBORN (HDN) — Rh− mother carrying Rh+ baby may produce anti-Rh antibodies that attack subsequent Rh+ pregnancies. Prevented now by RhoGAM injection.

questions.stem: If an Rh-NEGATIVE mother carries an Rh-POSITIVE fetus, the major risk is:

options.option_text: Rapid placental detachment in early pregnancy
Hemolytic disease of the newborn in subsequent pregnancies
Diabetes mellitus in the mother postpartum
Hypertension in the developing fetus immediately

questions.explanation: First Rh+ pregnancy — usually fine; mother gets sensitised at delivery (when fetal RBCs may enter maternal circulation) → produces anti-Rh antibodies. Subsequent Rh+ pregnancies — antibodies cross placenta → attack fetal RBCs → HEMOLYTIC DISEASE of NEWBORN (HDN, also called erythroblastosis fetalis): jaundice, anaemia, hydrops fetalis. PREVENTION: RhoGAM (anti-D immunoglobulin) injection given at 28 weeks + within 72 hr of delivery prevents maternal sensitisation. Lifesaving discovery.

questions.stem: The blood group inheritance follows MULTIPLE-ALLELE pattern. The IA, IB, and i alleles relate as:

options.option_text: All three equally co-dominant in any pairing
IA and IB co-dominant; both dominant over i
i is dominant over both IA and IB equally
Only IA is dominant; IB and i are recessive

questions.explanation: Three alleles: IA (codes for A antigen), IB (codes for B antigen), i (codes for nothing). IA + IB are CO-DOMINANT (both expressed in heterozygotes → AB blood group); both DOMINANT over i. Genotypes: AA or AO → A; BB or BO → B; AB → AB; OO → O. Provides classic example of multiple alleles + co-dominance taught in textbooks. Distractor 1 — only IA + IB are co-dominant. Distractor 3, 4 — wrong dominance hierarchy.

questions.stem: Approximately how many litres of blood does an adult human body contain?

options.option_text: 1 to 2 litres of blood total
5 to 6 litres of blood total
10 to 12 litres of blood total
20 litres of blood total

questions.explanation: Adult — ~5-6 litres blood (about 7-8% of body weight). Composition: PLASMA (~55%, mostly water + proteins), RBCs (~45%, packed cell volume / haematocrit), WBCs + platelets (~1%). Voluntary blood donation (~350 mL per session) — safe; body replaces fluid in 24 hr, RBCs in 6-8 weeks. Donate every 3 months (males) / 4 months (females). Distractor 1 too low. Distractor 3, 4 too high.
